source.title: Blender Transparent Glass Material using Principled BSDF Node

negative_controls.case: my first (wrong) reading 0.096 added as a second final for transparent.base_s
only the wrong 0.096 reading as final, single frame

visual_only_facts_not_in_transcript: transparent base saturation settles at 0.000 (narration: 'light grey, value 0.8')
frosted roughness drag passes 0.509 and 0.491 before 0.500

execution.application: Blender 5.2.2 LTS headless, Cycles OPTIX on RTX 5090
execution.version_gap: tutorial UI is Principled BSDF v1 (3.x); executed on v2 socket names (Transmission Weight, Specular IOR Level); Transmission Roughness has no v2 socket and its value was 0
execution.structural: readback.json socket values equal typed-state for all three materials (run2 == run3 == run3b)
execution.stand_in_scene: cube/backdrop/area light/camera are NOT tutorial evidence; built in a previous video that was not watched

judge.brief: side-by-side: score only how well RIGHT cube's glass material matches LEFT (tutorial) cube; ignore background/camera/lighting/UI

run2_white_set.note: first transparent/frosted scores (7/4) used swapped reference frames and were discarded; see superseded/

judge.repair: only the stand-in set changed (world/backdrop colour, light energy, 1024 samples); materials were never touched
judge.bounded_conclusion: The on-screen values were recovered, type-checked and executed; the materials read back exactly. Visual match is partial (6-8/10) and the judge's remaining complaints (edge sharpness, depth) are scene/camera, which the tutorial never showed. This does not establish tutorial-to-skill reliability in general.

determinism.blender_cycles: run3 vs run3b: PNG hashes differ; ImageMagick RMSE 1.37e-5 .. 1.42e-5 normalized (seed 0, OPTIX + denoiser is not bit-exact)

incidents: reference frames for transparent/frosted were swapped on first crop (2.5s title is the CLEAR cube, 7.5s title is the FROSTED cube); fixed by re-reading both frames side by side; wrong files kept in superseded/
Blender wrote run1 renders to C:\run1 because the relative output path was resolved against the Blender working dir; fixed with .resolve(); stray files left for the owner to remove
